scope: Static emplacement and carried-weapon authority during native flight and simulation dormancy
sourceIntent: LAMBS treats native fleeing as forced work outside ordinary danger decisions. Static deployment is useful group support but must compose with that actor-level authority. No upstream delayed inventory/physics shortcut is copied.
finding: CombatEffective excludes injury/captivity, not fleeing/hidden/dormant states. StaticSupport and StaticDeploy omitted those states in recruitment, active participant checks, release and native assembly callbacks. They could issue boarding/equipment/follow work while those states owned the actor.
implementation: Reject fleeing, hidden or simulation-disabled actors in new emplacement and carried-team candidate selection. Existing temporary retry policy stays unchanged.

An active emplacement actor yields via existing metadata retirement. Deployment participant checks retire when a reserved actor enters those states. Existing release gates veto native writes over affected actors.
WeaponAssembled and WeaponDisassembled callbacks recheck actual actors before adopting results or issuing equipment work. Original phase deadlines and exact handlers remain.
Existing short bag approach repeats the same live actor boundary. No new scan, callback, timer, helper or global CombatEffective semantic change.

validation.provenance: Unsigned dirty development snapshot retaining unrelated dirt; review and handover notes afterward. Initial focused callback slice stopped at an earlier conditional; test slice corrected to actual callback body.

limits: No physical flight, late assembly, interrupted boarding, packing, locality or runtime performance acceptance.
Retiring CBE markers and handlers does not prove an already-issued engine action is quiescent. Physical equipment stays in the world; no forced inventory rollback.
Audits remain paused. No push, merge, CI dispatch, release or upload. No whole-mod parity or percentage claim.
